metadata.notes: A generic verb, added 2026-08-16, closing TWO independently-named real gaps at once rather than being built single-purpose for either: (1) par-fry.json's own restNote — the cited ~10-minute rest between PAR_FRY and the finishing FRY, previously impossible to express in any RecipeScript at all (see crispy-french-fries.json's restGapNote); (2) the tortilla-de-patatas.json family's combine-then-rest step, where a user directly identified this repo was missing it (see tortilla_mixture.json's restNote for the specific technique this closes). addsTag: 'rested' (orthogonal, like SALT/PEPPER — resting doesn't change WHAT an instance is, just adds a real fact about its recent history) rather than a new transformedState, since nothing about the target's FORM changes during a rest, only time passing.
metadata.genericityNote: Deliberately entity-agnostic (isRestable capability, not a fixed target list) precisely because 'let it sit before the next step' is a real technique that recurs across genuinely unrelated dishes for genuinely different underlying physical reasons (moisture/heat redistribution in a fried potato vs. residual-heat protein setting + flavor absorption in a raw-egg mixture) — this action does not attempt to model WHY resting matters for any specific entity (informational only, same non-causal depth as every other timing parameter in this vocabulary); each entity's own metadata documents its own specific reason, this file just provides the shared mechanism.
metadata.durationSecondsNote: 300-1800s (5-30 minutes) spans both real cited use cases: par-fry.json's own source specifies 'at least 10 minutes' (600s) for the par-fry-to-fry rest; tortilla de patatas' combine-to-fry rest is commonly cited across multiple convergent consumer recipe sources (Spanish Sabores, Kitchen Frau, and others) at anywhere from 5 to 20 minutes (300-1200s) — see REFERENCES.md. The two ranges overlap rather than being identical, which is expected: they're different techniques for different reasons that happen to share the same verb, not one universal 'correct' resting time.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): purely elapsed-time passing with no discrete completion signal beyond the clock itself — the clearest possible case for actionKind: 'continuous' under the paper's own test, even though (unlike BOIL/SIMMER/FRY) nothing here is actively driven by a heat source. verification.method: 'elapsed_time_only' reflects the same fact from VerificationCriterionSchema's own enum — there is no visual/thermal/tactile signal to check, only whether the clock ran out.
metadata.maxDurationSecondsNote: Reused directly from this action's own already-cited durationSeconds.numericRange.max (1800s) — same convention as fry.json's/par-fry.json's identically-named notes.

verification.description: No physical change to check for — confirm the stated duration has actually elapsed since the previous step
